question: Across FLEX and FLEX-2, at what oxygen levels did droplet flames go out (extinction)?
claim: In FLEX (PSI-69), 186 microgravity droplet tests ended in flame extinction at oxygen levels from 12% to 30% O2, spread over 13 distinct O2 levels, while the FLEX-2 (PSI-68) table records no test outcome (0 rows with an outcome), so it cannot say where its flames went out.
summary_student: On the space station, FLEX burned single fuel droplets and 186 of those flames went out on their own, at oxygen levels anywhere from 12% to 30%. FLEX-2 also burned droplets at oxygen levels from 17% to 30%, but its data table only lists the conditions it tried, not whether each flame went out, so it does not answer this question.
summary_professional: PSI-69 (FLEX) experimental table: n = 186 tests with Test end = extinction, initial ambient O2 mole fraction from 12% to 30% O2 across 13 distinct O2 levels, with N2, N2+CO2 or N2+He diluents, all in microgravity. PSI-68 (FLEX-2) experimental table is a condition matrix (O2 tested from 17% to 30% O2) with no outcome column: 0 rows with an outcome, so no FLEX-2 extinction oxygen level can be derived from PSI. The 12% to 30% range describes where extinction was observed, not a limiting oxygen index.

params.sql: SELECT 'flex_extinction_o2_min' AS name, min(o2_pct_min) AS value, '% O2' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_min')) AS source_columns FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-69' AND outcome = 'extinction' AND o2_pct_min IS NOT NULL GROUP BY investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT 'flex_extinction_o2_max', max(o2_pct_max), '% O2', investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row), list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_max')) FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-69' AND outcome = 'extinction' AND o2_pct_max IS NOT NULL GROUP BY investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT 'flex_extinction_tests', count(*), 'tests', investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row), list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.outcome')) FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-69' AND outcome = 'extinction' GROUP BY investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT 'flex_extinction_o2_levels', count(DISTINCT o2_pct_min), 'distinct O2 levels', investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row), list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_min')) FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-69' AND outcome = 'extinction' AND o2_pct_min IS NOT NULL GROUP BY investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT 'flex2_rows_with_outcome', count(outcome), 'rows', investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row), flatten(list(DISTINCT json_keys(raw))) FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-68' GROUP BY investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT 'flex2_o2_tested_min', min(o2_pct_min), '% O2', investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row), list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_min')) FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-68' AND o2_pct_min IS NOT NULL GROUP BY investigation, source_table UNION ALL SELECT 'flex2_o2_tested_max', max(o2_pct_max), '% O2', investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row), list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.o2_pct_max')) FROM tests WHERE investigation = 'PSI-68' AND o2_pct_max IS NOT NULL GROUP BY investigation, source_table

method.formula: The values returned by the SQL query in params, one row per value, each with the source rows it used.

columns: O initial ambient composition; mole fraction

assumptions: A FLEX test counts as an extinction when its Test end column reads extinction; tests ending in completion or disruption are excluded.
Oxygen is the initial ambient O2 mole fraction, treated as equal to volume percent.
FLEX headers lost their subscripts in PSI's file, so the O column is read as O2.
limitations: FLEX-2 gives no per-test outcome, so this finding says nothing about where FLEX-2 flames went out.
The range covers all FLEX fuels, diluents, droplet sizes and pressures together; it is not an extinction limit for any one fuel or condition.
Extinction at a given oxygen level does not mean flames cannot survive there: other FLEX tests at overlapping levels ended in completion or disruption.
All tests are microgravity droplet flames; the finding does not cover solids, gases, partial gravity or Earth gravity.

chart.idea: Bar chart of FLEX extinction tests per O2 level from 12% to 30% O2, next to a range bar of the O2 levels FLEX-2 tested with no outcome recorded.

graph.idea: Proof graph linking this finding to FLEX and FLEX-2, which share the MDCA droplet hardware, and to their PSI tables.
